scenarios.depth_note: Tests itemized bill auditing, chargemaster price spotting, and dispute scripting
scenarios.prompt: Got a $14,320 ER bill after a dislocated shoulder — 4 hours, one X-ray, no surgery. Tell me which line items are inflated, what each should actually cost, and exactly what to say to the billing department to get it reduced.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests uninsured cash-rate negotiation and lump-sum settlement strategy
scenarios.prompt: The ER billed me $8,900 for stitches and a CT scan, but I was uninsured that night. What should the cash-pay price be, what's a fair lump-sum settlement offer within 30 days, and who do I call to negotiate it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests facility-fee breakdown between hospital and ambulatory surgery center
scenarios.prompt: I need a knee arthroscopy. The hospital quoted $28,500 all-in, the ambulatory surgery center quoted $11,200. Break down where the $17,300 difference comes from — surgeon, anesthesia, facility fees — and tell me if the cheaper option is actually safe for this procedure.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests in-network vs out-of-network true out-of-pocket math
scenarios.prompt: My insurer says the hospital is in-network but the surgery center is out-of-network for my gallbladder removal. The hospital wants $6,400 out of pocket; the center wants $3,900 flat cash. After my $2,000 deductible and 20% coinsurance, which one actually costs me less?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests insurance session-limit vs cash-pay package comparison
scenarios.prompt: I need 16 PT sessions for my back at $180 each. Insurance covers 12 a year with a $40 copay. The clinic offers all 16 cash for a $2,200 package. Do the math — which route is cheaper, and by how much?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests deductible timing strategy across plan years
scenarios.prompt: It's October and I haven't touched my $3,000 deductible. My ortho ordered 20 PT sessions at $175 each and I can't finish them before December. How do I split them across this year and next so I don't pay full price twice?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests EAP, deductible, and coinsurance layering for a year of therapy
scenarios.prompt: Therapy costs $200 a session. My plan has a $2,500 mental-health deductible, then covers 70%. My employer EAP gives 6 free sessions. Map out my cheapest path for weekly sessions over the next 12 months, month by month.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests mental health parity appeal for out-of-network denials
scenarios.prompt: My out-of-network therapist charges $225 a session and my claim for 12 sessions was denied. The in-network option has a 4-month wait. Walk me through a parity-law appeal — what documentation I need and what to actually write in the letter.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests lifetime-cost comparison with replacement cycles
scenarios.prompt: Lost a molar. Implant is $4,800, bridge is $3,200. I'm 34. Bridges last 10–15 years, implants 25+. What's the 30-year total cost of each including replacements, and which is actually cheaper?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests dental annual-max sequencing across benefit years
scenarios.prompt: My dental plan maxes at $1,500 a year. The implant needs 3 stages over 6 months: extraction ($400), bone graft ($900), implant plus crown ($4,800). Schedule the stages across this year and next to maximize insurance and minimize my cash.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests lump-sum discount vs 0% plan math combined with FSA
scenarios.prompt: Braces for my kid: $6,800 total. The office offers 0% for 24 months or 5% off for paying upfront. I have $2,750 in my FSA this year. What's the smartest payment combo, and can I even use an FSA for orthodontics?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests phased two-child orthodontics payment timeline
scenarios.prompt: Two kids need braces at $7,200 each — one now, one in 18 months. I have a $3,050 FSA and the office won't start kid two until kid one's plan is half paid. Build me a payment timeline that doesn't wreck my monthly budget.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests LASIK breakeven vs lifetime glasses and contacts cost
scenarios.prompt: LASIK is $4,600 for both eyes. I spend $520 a year on contacts plus $240 every two years on glasses. I'm 29 with a stable prescription. How many years until LASIK pays for itself, and is it worth doing at my age?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests HSA eligibility and lifetime enhancement warranty value
scenarios.prompt: The LASIK center charges $4,200 base plus $600 for a lifetime enhancement warranty. Can I pay with my HSA, and is the enhancement plan statistically worth it or just margin for the clinic?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests prior-auth denial appeal letter with clinical language
scenarios.prompt: My $1,900-a-month asthma biologic was denied — the insurer says I must fail two cheaper inhalers first. I've already failed one and the other gave me bad side effects. Draft my appeal letter with the exact clinical language that gets these approved.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests step-therapy exception and bridge-supply tactics against a deadline
scenarios.prompt: My rheumatologist prescribed a $3,400-a-month drug that needs prior auth and step therapy. I have 9 pills left — about 9 days. What do I do right now so I don't gap: emergency fill, doctor samples, manufacturer bridge program, or appealing the step therapy?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests nonprofit hospital financial assistance eligibility math
scenarios.prompt: I owe $22,000 to a nonprofit hospital after a 4-day stay. I make $58,000 a year supporting a family of two. Am I eligible for charity care under their financial assistance policy, and how do I apply before they send it to collections?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests collection-stage negotiation: settlement vs hardship plan
scenarios.prompt: A $6,700 ambulance bill went to collections and they're demanding $558 a month for 12 months, which I can't afford. What's my realistic play — lump-sum settlement at 40%, a hardship plan, or disputing the charge?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests predictable-expense allocation across FSA and HSA
scenarios.prompt: Next year I'll spend $3,000 I can predict: $1,800 on my kid's orthodontics, $900 on therapy copays, $300 on prescriptions. I have both an FSA and an HSA. How much do I put in each, and in what order do I spend it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests use-it-or-lose-it FSA spend-down strategy
scenarios.prompt: I have $1,400 left in my FSA with 6 weeks left in the year — use it or lose it, no rollover. I wear contacts and need new glasses. What's the smartest way to spend it down on things I'll actually use?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests waiver eligibility across Common App, Coalition, and direct applications
scenarios.prompt: I'm applying to 9 colleges at $75–$90 each — about $750 in fees I don't have. I qualify for free lunch. Which waiver forms do I need for Common App vs Coalition vs the two schools that take neither, and what's the actual process for each?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests CSS Profile fee waiver stacking with FAFSA
scenarios.prompt: FAFSA is free, but 6 of my schools require the CSS Profile — $25 for the first school, $16 for each additional one. Is there a fee waiver for the CSS Profile too, and do I have to do anything different to get it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests articulation agreement credit-transfer math
scenarios.prompt: Community college costs $4,200 a year vs $31,000 at the state university I want to graduate from. If I do 2 years at CC then transfer, which credits actually transfer under the state articulation agreement, and what's my real total savings?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests transfer scholarship timing and GPA thresholds
scenarios.prompt: I'm at community college with a 3.6 GPA, planning to transfer to State U next fall. There's a $5,000-a-year transfer scholarship requiring a 3.5 GPA and a February 1 application. What else do I need to line up right now so I don't lose money in the transfer?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests per-semester buy-vs-rent math with resale value
scenarios.prompt: My chemistry textbook is $289 new, $95 to rent per semester, $180 used. It's a two-semester sequence. Run the numbers: buy new and resell, buy used, or rent twice?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests open-textbook and library-reserve alternatives before spending
scenarios.prompt: My 5 classes need $640 in textbooks total and I'm broke. Before I buy anything, tell me what to check: open textbooks, library reserves, older editions — and how to figure out which professors actually use the book.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests servicer transfer audit and autopay continuity
scenarios.prompt: My $34,000 in federal loans just moved to a new servicer and my autopay stopped. My first payment under the new servicer is due in 3 weeks. What do I verify so I don't miss a payment or lose my income-driven plan in the transfer?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests misapplied-payment correction with a new servicer
scenarios.prompt: My new servicer applied my $412 payment to interest and fees instead of principal like my old one did, and my balance barely moved. How do I get this fixed and make sure future payments hit principal the way I want?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests recertification timing after a mid-year raise
scenarios.prompt: My income-driven plan recertification is due March 15. I got a raise from $52k to $71k in November, and my payment will jump from $210 to $480 if I recertify now. Is there any legal timing strategy here, or do I just recertify and take the hit?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests missed-deadline consequences and late recertification
scenarios.prompt: I missed my income-driven recertification deadline last month and my servicer moved me to the standard plan at $690 a month. What happens to my accrued interest, and can I still recertify late to get back on the plan?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests qualifying-payment count audit and employer certification gaps
scenarios.prompt: I've worked at a nonprofit hospital for 6 years making payments the whole time, but my PSLF count only shows 58 qualifying payments. Walk me through auditing which payments got disqualified and how to get the missing ones certified.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests PSLF buyback program value for forbearance months
scenarios.prompt: I have 104 qualifying PSLF payments but spent 16 months in forbearance that don't count. There's a buyback program now — is it worth buying back those months at my current income-driven payment amount to reach 120?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests SECURE 2.0 rollover eligibility rules
scenarios.prompt: My daughter's 529 has $18,000 left over and she's done with college. I heard I can roll it into a Roth IRA now. What are the actual rules — the 15-year account requirement, the $35,000 lifetime cap, the annual limit interaction — and does she need earned income?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests multi-year rollover sequencing under annual limits
scenarios.prompt: There's $30,000 left in the 529. The Roth rollover is capped at $35,000 lifetime but limited to the annual IRA contribution each year. Map out the year-by-year rollover schedule and explain what happens to the earnings portion for taxes.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests outside-scholarship displacement policy and loan-reduction requests
scenarios.prompt: I won a $5,000 local scholarship, but my college says it will reduce my $8,000 need-based grant dollar for dollar — making the scholarship worthless to me. Is that allowed, and can I ask them to reduce my loans instead?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests scholarship deferral and stacking strategy
scenarios.prompt: I have $12,000 in outside scholarships but my school displaces grants first. Can I defer some scholarships to sophomore year, or ask the scholarship organizations to cover things the school doesn't count, like a laptop or study abroad?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests after-tax earnings and FAFSA income-protection comparison
scenarios.prompt: I was offered $2,800 a year in work-study at $14 an hour on campus, or I could work 15 hours a week at Target for $17 an hour. Which leaves me with more money after taxes, and how does each affect next year's FAFSA?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests hours-cap and commute tradeoff for off-campus work
scenarios.prompt: Work-study caps me at 12 hours a week, but an off-campus dining hall job pays $3 more an hour with no cap. I need $400 a month. Do the real math including the 25-minute commute and the FAFSA impact.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests debt-to-salary ratio and 10-year ROI by degree field
scenarios.prompt: I'm choosing between a $68,000 master's in data science and a $45,000 master's in social work. Median starting salaries are $112k and $58k. Run the 10-year ROI including loan interest — is either one actually worth it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests employer-tuition part-time vs full-time program tradeoff
scenarios.prompt: My employer will pay $10,000 a year toward a part-time MBA ($72,000 total over 3 years), but I have an offer for a full-time program ($95,000 over 2 years, no income while enrolled). Which path has the better 5-year net outcome?
